{"parentUuid":"fc933295-2de3-441b-8fd7-c5fe006c85d2","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Claude Docs"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: \"<root id>\"`."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"a0fdec5a-bd17-45f6-96b1-528138de17b3","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:31:14.588Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\n# MCP Server Instructions\n\nThe following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:\n\n## claude.ai Claude Docs\nClaude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: \"<root id>\"`.\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"a0fdec5a-bd17-45f6-96b1-528138de17b3","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like \"how do I do X\", \"find a skill for X\", \"is there a skill that can...\", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.\n- mattpocock-skills:diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says \"diagnose\"/\"debug this\", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.\n- mattpocock-skills:tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \"red-green-refactor\", or wants integration tests.\n- mattpocock-skills:prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.\n- mattpocock-skills:research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.\n- mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\n- mattpocock-skills:codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.\n- mattpocock-skills:code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".\n- mattpocock-skills:resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.\n- mattpocock-skills:wizard: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.\n- mattpocock-skills:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\n- mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch\n- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or \"your own browser\"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.\n- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for \"computer use\". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.\n- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. {"parentUuid":"aab945ad-5a2f-45d7-85cd-c88de8ae448a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e4a8ea0e-57e4-4cfe-a3ff-dbeed42dc0e9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01THj95AxPcTniiM7QXSVxgU","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# CONTEXT.md glossary\n2\t\n3\t## Content\n4\t\n5\t**Post**\n6\tA dated piece of writing with a title, a Markdown body, a status, an author and timestamps. Posts are for things that need to go out quickly.\n7\t\n8\t**Slug**\n9\tThe URL-safe form of a title, such as `afrobeat-night`. A Post's slug is generated from its title on the first save, with a number added if it already exists. Editors never enter it. It does not change when the title or event details are corrected, so shared links keep working. Only the Admin may change a slug, and is warned that this can break an old link. A Page's slug is also Admin-only.\n10\t\n11\t**Event announcement**\n12\tA Post that announces an event, such as the Afrobeat event. It has no event-date field of its own. The event's date, time, location and who can attend are written clearly in the body. _Avoid_: \"Event\" as a separate kind of content.\n13\t\n14\t**Announcements**\n15\tThe public list of Published Posts, ordered by First-published date, newest first. The Home page shows the five most recent, with a link to the full list. It is not \"Upcoming Events\": newest Posts are not necessarily future events. _Avoid_: \"Upcoming Events\" for this list.\n16\t\n17\t**First-published date**\n18\tThe date a Post was first Published. Announcements are ordered by it, newest first, and each Event card shows it. It is kept if the Post is unpublished and later Published again. It is never labeled as the event's date: the event's actual date and time stay in the Body.\n19\t\n20\t**Updated date**\n21\tShown on an Event card when a Post's content changes after it was first Published, so visitors can tell details were corrected. Editing does not reorder the Announcements list.\n22\t\n23\t**Page**\n24\tPermanent content, such as information about ASA and cultural resources. A published Page appears in the public navigation.\n25\t\n26\t**Photo**\n27\tAn image shown inside a Post or Page. Photos are not uploaded through a separate feature and there is no gallery. Every photo has descriptive alt text. An Editor writes the caption, alt text and Markdown reference but cannot add a new image file alone: the release-holder adds approved image files, and publishing copies them into the public site. Demo illustrations are labeled as illustrative and have usable rights.\n28\t\n29\t**Photos page**\n30\tA Page that collects selected photos from past activities.\n31\t\n32\t**Photo permission**\n33\tA working rule for this project: an ASA leader checks that ASA has permission to use a real photo before it is added to a Post or Page. ASA's formal approval process, if any, is unknown and is not described here. The class demo uses placeholders or images we have permission to use.\n34\t\n35\t**Author**\n36\tThe account that wrote a Post. Recorded in the admin console for every Post.\n37\t\n38\t**Display name**\n39\tThe public name shown as a Post's byline, set by the Admin when creating the account. It can be a name, a nickname or a team name such as \"ASA Events Team\", so no member's real name is public without their agreement. _Avoid_: showing the **Username** as the byline.\n40\t\n41\t**Deactivated account**\n42\tAn account whose owner can no longer sign in. Its published Posts stay public and the original Author relationship is kept. If a former member wants their name removed, the Admin changes the account's Display name (for example to \"ASA Events Team\"). Accounts are deactivated, never deleted.\n43\t\n44\t**Username**\n45\tThe private name an account signs in with. It is never shown publicly as a byline by default.\n46\t\n47\t## Public site\n48\t\n49\t**Home page**\n50\tA short Welcome text followed by the latest Announcements.\n51\t\n52\t**Welcome text**\n53\tThe short greeting at the top of the Home page. It uses the wording from `notes/client-brief.md`: ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. No other claims about ASA are made.\n54\t\n55\t**Navigation**\n56\tThe public menu: Announcements plus every published Page. The starter Pages for the demo are About ASA, Resources and Photos. They are placeholders, not a claim about ASA's real pages.\n57\t\n58\t**Event card**\n59\tHow an Announcement appears in the Announcements list. It is clear and readable on a phone.\n60\t\n61\t**Decorative graphic**\n62\tA licensed image or graphic used for looks only. It is never presented as a photo of a real ASA event. Until ASA has permission for real photos, the Photos page says that actual event photos will be added then.\n63\t\n64\t## Admin console\n65\t\n66\t**Dashboard**\n67\tThe first screen after signing in. It shows four content counts: Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages. Only the Admin also sees the number of active accounts and Deactivated accounts. It carries a clear reminder that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run. It has no \"Changes not live yet\" indicator unless the app can determine that reliably. It stays simple on a phone.\n68\t\n69\t**Content list**\n70\tOne list of Posts and Pages, filtered by type (Post or Page) and by status (Draft or Published). Each row shows title, status, Display name and last-updated time.\n71\t\n72\t## Writing\n73\t\n74\t**Body**\n75\tThe Markdown text of a Post or Page. Allowed: headings, emphasis, lists, links, and images with alt text. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms are stripped and never run. Sanitizing happens in both the Preview and the public export.\n76\t\n77\t**Preview**\n78\tThe editor's view of a Post or Page. It shows the same rendered, sanitized content as the public page, not a separate approximation.\n79\t\n80\t**Event details hint**\n81\tA short hint near the Post editor suggesting the body cover What, When, Where and Who can attend. It is not pre-filled into the body, and an Editor can hide it without deleting any content.\n82\t\n83\t## Publishing\n84\t\n85\t**Published**\n86\tA status in the admin console meaning a Post or Page is ready for the public site. It is not yet visible to visitors. Drafts are never Published and never leave the database.\n87\t\n88\t**Live**\n89\tVisible to visitors: someone has run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` after the content was marked Published. _Avoid_: saying \"published\" when you mean Live.\n90\t\n91\t**Release checklist**\n92\tA short, repeatable list of steps for making Published content Live. It also states the limit that an Editor cannot add a new image file alone, and is where Photo permission is confirmed before a real photo is added. For the class demo, the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n93\t\n94\t## Roles\n95\t\n96\t**Admin**\n97\tAn ASA leader. Manages accounts and permanent Pages: creates and deletes Pages, publishes or unpublishes them, and changes Page titles or slugs (which affect navigation and links). An Admin cannot deactivate their own account, and the last active Admin cannot be demoted, so the console is never left without someone able to manage accounts.\n98\t\n99\t**Editor**\n100\tAnother ASA member. Creates and publishes Posts directly, because speed matters for announcements. May edit any Post, including another editor's, so event details can be corrected close to the event. May not delete a Post; only the Admin can. May update the body of an existing Page, so the Photos page can stay current, but may not create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page. This is a design choice for the ASA site, not something observed in WordPress.\n101\t\n102\t**Permission refusal**\n103\tWhat an Editor sees on any attempt at an Admin-only action, whether by button, typed address or direct submission: a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard. Admin-only controls are also hidden from an Editor's normal screens, but hiding is never the protection. Editors may manage Posts and update the body of existing Pages; they may not manage users, delete content, change Page structure or publication status, or change slugs.\n104\t\n105\t**Password reset**\n106\tThe only way to recover a lost password. The Admin sets a new password for an existing account and cannot view the old one. The new password is stored hashed and is never printed or logged. The Admin passes it to the account owner outside the CMS through a trusted channel. There is no email link and no self-service reset.\n107\t\n108\t## Out of scope for this version\n109\t\n110\tMentioned as possible later features, not built now.\n111\t\n112\t- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n113\t- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n114\t- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n115\t- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n116\t- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n117\t- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n118\t- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n119\t- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n120\t"}]},"uuid":"8e214c82-591d-4bdd-9e1a-97dbf89e9fc8","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:31:16.612Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**\nA dated piece of writing with a title, a Markdown body, a status, an author and timestamps. Every photo has descriptive alt text. An Editor writes the caption, alt text and Markdown reference but cannot add a new image file alone: the release-holder adds approved image files, and publishing copies them into the public site. Demo illustrations are labeled as illustrative and have usable rights.\n\n**Photos page**\nA Page that collects selected photos from past activities.\n\n**Photo permission**\nA working rule for this project: an ASA leader checks that ASA has permission to use a real photo before it is added to a Post or Page. ASA's formal approval process, if any, is unknown and is not described here. The class demo uses placeholders or images we have permission to use.\n\n**Author**\nThe account that wrote a Post. Recorded in the admin console for every Post.\n\n**Display name**\nThe public name shown as a Post's byline, set by the Admin when creating the account. It can be a name, a nickname or a team name such as \"ASA Events Team\", so no member's real name is public without their agreement. _Avoid_: showing the **Username** as the byline.\n\n**Deactivated account**\nAn account whose owner can no longer sign in. Its published Posts stay public and the original Author relationship is kept. If a former member wants their name removed, the Admin changes the account's Display name (for example to \"ASA Events Team\"). Accounts are deactivated, never deleted.\n\n**Username**\nThe private name an account signs in with. It is never shown publicly as a byline by default.\n\n## Public site\n\n**Home page**\nA short Welcome text followed by the latest Announcements.\n\n**Welcome text**\nThe short greeting at the top of the Home page. It uses the wording from `notes/client-brief.md`: ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community. No other claims about ASA are made.\n\n**Navigation**\nThe public menu: Announcements plus every published Page. The starter Pages for the demo are About ASA, Resources and Photos. They are placeholders, not a claim about ASA's real pages.\n\n**Event card**\nHow an Announcement appears in the Announcements list. It is clear and readable on a phone.\n\n**Decorative graphic**\nA licensed image or graphic used for looks only. It is never presented as a photo of a real ASA event. Until ASA has permission for real photos, the Photos page says that actual event photos will be added then.\n\n## Admin console\n\n**Dashboard**\nThe first screen after signing in. It shows four content counts: Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages and Draft Pages. Only the Admin also sees the number of active accounts and Deactivated accounts. It carries a clear reminder that marking content Published does not make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run. It has no \"Changes not live yet\" indicator unless the app can determine that reliably. It stays simple on a phone.\n\n**Content list**\nOne list of Posts and Pages, filtered by type (Post or Page) and by status (Draft or Published). Each row shows title, status, Display name and last-updated time.\n\n## Writing\n\n**Body**\nThe Markdown text of a Post or Page. Allowed: headings, emphasis, lists, links, and images with alt text. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms are stripped and never run. Sanitizing happens in both the Preview and the public export.\n\n**Preview**\nThe editor's view of a Post or Page. It shows the same rendered, sanitized content as the public page, not a separate approximation.\n\n**Event details hint**\nA short hint near the Post editor suggesting the body cover What, When, Where and Who can attend. It is not pre-filled into the body, and an Editor can hide it without deleting any content.\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Published**\nA status in the admin console meaning a Post or Page is ready for the public site. It is not yet visible to visitors. Drafts are never Published and never leave the database.\n\n**Live**\nVisible to visitors: someone has run `cms publish` and `cms deploy` after the content was marked Published. _Avoid_: saying \"published\" when you mean Live.\n\n**Release checklist**\nA short, repeatable list of steps for making Published content Live. It also states the limit that an Editor cannot add a new image file alone, and is where Photo permission is confirmed before a real photo is added. For the class demo, the project author runs it from their own laptop. ASA has no known person responsible for this step, and none is assumed.\n\n## Roles\n\n**Admin**\nAn ASA leader. Manages accounts and permanent Pages: creates and deletes Pages, publishes or unpublishes them, and changes Page titles or slugs (which affect navigation and links). An Admin cannot deactivate their own account, and the last active Admin cannot be demoted, so the console is never left without someone able to manage accounts.\n\n**Editor**\nAnother ASA member. Creates and publishes Posts directly, because speed matters for announcements. May edit any Post, including another editor's, so event details can be corrected close to the event. May not delete a Post; only the Admin can. May update the body of an existing Page, so the Photos page can stay current, but may not create, delete, publish, unpublish, retitle or re-slug a Page. This is a design choice for the ASA site, not something observed in WordPress.\n\n**Permission refusal**\nWhat an Editor sees on any attempt at an Admin-only action, whether by button, typed address or direct submission: a clear \"You don't have permission\" page with a link back to the dashboard. Admin-only controls are also hidden from an Editor's normal screens, but hiding is never the protection. Editors may manage Posts and update the body of existing Pages; they may not manage users, delete content, change Page structure or publication status, or change slugs.\n\n**Password reset**\nThe only way to recover a lost password. The Admin sets a new password for an existing account and cannot view the old one. The new password is stored hashed and is never printed or logged. The Admin passes it to the account owner outside the CMS through a trusted channel. There is no email link and no self-service reset.\n\n## Out of scope for this version\n\nMentioned as possible later features, not built now.\n\n- A separate Event content type, an event-date field, and automatic upcoming/past sorting.\n- Photo upload forms, automatic gallery management, and photo approvals enforced by software. (The Photos page with approved images is in scope.)\n- Account deletion, and a first-login password change flow.\n- Email sending, including email-based password reset.\n- A \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- RSVPs and sign-ups, comments, search, and tags or categories.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page building, and a rich-text WYSIWYG editor.\n- Any claim about ASA's real history, members, leaders, schedule or approval process.\n","numLines":120,"startLine":1,"totalLines":120}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"aab945ad-5a2f-45d7-85cd-c88de8ae448a","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"5203225a-80fd-49a7-a8d2-e67a62b54325","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e4a8ea0e-57e4-4cfe-a3ff-dbeed42dc0e9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019c6GVgwX4XuLHb9RtF5m6U","type":"tool_result","content":"{\"body\":\"## Parent\\n\\nSpec: #1\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nThe public site looks polished and welcoming to a first-time visitor and works on a phone. The Home page shows a short Welcome text and the five most recent Announcements as clear Event cards, with a link to all of them. Photos inside Posts and Pages appear with alt text. The site is accessible.\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n- [ ] The Home page shows the Welcome text, using only the client brief's wording (a student group primarily for African students and students with African backgrounds, welcoming anyone interested in African cultures and community), followed by the five most recent Published Announcements and a link to the full Announcements page.\\n- [ ] Each Announcement appears as an Event card showing its title, First-published date and byline. If the content changed after first publishing, the card also shows an \\\"Updated\\\" date. The First-published date is never labelled as the event date.\\n- [ ] A Post that is unpublished and Published again keeps its original First-published date and position.\\n- [ ] Approved image files added to the project by the release-holder are copied into the export by `cms publish`, and Markdown image references resolve with relative paths. An Editor writes only the caption, alt text and reference.\\n- [ ] The Photos page shows placeholder or rights-cleared demo images labelled as illustrative, and says that actual event photos will be added when ASA has permission to use them. Nothing presents a stock photo or illustration as a real ASA event.\\n- [ ] Accessibility: a sensible heading order on every page, readable colour contrast, visible focus and full keyboard access, a layout that works at about 390 px, and alt text on every image.\\n- [ ] Only relative paths appear in the export, and Drafts never appear.\\n- [ ] Tests at the published-site seam cover the five-item Home page, the link to all Announcements, cards with First-published and Updated dates, image copying with relative paths, alt text on every image, heading order, and the Welcome text. No claim about ASA beyond the brief appears anywhere in the export.\\n\\n## Blocked by\\n\\n- #4 (T03: blocking)\\n- #6 (T05: blocking)\\n\\n\",\"labels\":[{\"id\":\"LA_kwDOUxXkN88AAAAC5R34Jw\",\"name\":\"ready-for-agent\",\"description\":\"Triaged and ready for an agent to pick up\",\"color\":\"1d76db\"},{\"id\":\"LA_kwDOUxXkN88AAAAC5R7b9Q\",\"name\":\"ticket\",\"description\":\"Vertical-slice implementation ticket\",\"color\":\"5319e7\"}],\"number\":8,\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"title\":\"T07: Polished, accessible public site\"}\n----\nb29a37c70ec9ac7f46aca393c35a698644e904b9\nT07: Polished, accessible public site\n\n- Home page: Welcome text in a hero, five latest Event cards, link to all.\n- Stylesheet moved to templates/public/style.css: mobile-first, light and dark\n  tokens with contrast checked by tests, visible focus, skip link, aria-current.\n- cms publish copies approved image files from images/ into the export; {"parentUuid":"a9003e49-28d0-49db-8470-3648a7a2421d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e4a8ea0e-57e4-4cfe-a3ff-dbeed42dc0e9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Az1DVKpNoZwGBw7qXd6f7H","type":"tool_result","content":"app\nCLAUDE.md\ncms.db\nCONTEXT.md\ndocs\nimages\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nsite\ntemplates\ntests\nuv.lock\n----\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n----\n# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n\nClick **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\nDo not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n\n## Start here\n\n1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env\nuv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py   # demo accounts: admin, editor\nuv run --env-file .env cms serve    # then open http://localhost:8000/admin and sign in\n```\n\nSign in with the username `admin` (or `editor`) and the matching password from `.env`.\nTo create your own first Admin instead: set `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, then\n`uv run --env-file .env cms create-admin --username NAME --display-name \"ASA Leadership\"`.\nThe password is read from the environment and never printed.\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\nscripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\nimages/            approved image files the release-holder adds; `cms publish` copies them\ntests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\napp/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\ndocs/adr/          two example decision records\n```\n\nTwo functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\nBoth are graded. Use `/tdd`, as the manual says.\n\n## Deadlines\n\nStage 1 (`mp2-mvp` tag): Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm Eastern (soft target).\nStage 2 (`mp2-final` tag): Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern, grace until Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm.\n\nRun `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\n*(Required. Replace this section: name the models and skills you used, quote two\nprompts you really sent, describe one real model failure, and include a\n\"Backends used\" table if you ever switched providers.)*\n----\nT06-content-list-390px.png\nT06-dashboard-390px.png\nT07-home-390px.png\nT07-photos-390px.png\n!! .env\n!! cms.db\n!! site/","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"7878f7d2-ca09-436a-bb28-b778cd39287c","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:31:24.821Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"app\nCLAUDE.md\ncms.db\nCONTEXT.md\ndocs\nimages\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nsite\ntemplates\ntests\nuv.lock\n----\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n----\n# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n\nClick **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\nDo not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n\n## Start here\n\n1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. }\n  .hero { padding: 1.75rem 2rem 2rem; }\n}\n=== publish.py\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nTwo rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     Pages one folder down (posts/) reach the site root with a `root` of \"../\".\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import closing\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import pages, settings\nfrom app.db import connect\nfrom app.rendering import render_body\n\n# The wording comes from notes/client-brief.md. Make no other claim about ASA.\nWELCOME = (\n    \"ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students \"\n    \"with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African \"\n    \"cultures and community.\"\n)\nHOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS = 5\n# Approved image files the release-holder may add to images/. Anything else is ignored.\nIMAGE_SUFFIXES = {\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\", \".gif\", \".webp\", \".svg\"}\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef _day(timestamp: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"A stored UTC timestamp as (\"2026-09-28\", \"28 September 2026\").\"\"\"\n    moment = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp)\n    return moment.date().isoformat(), f\"{moment.day} {moment:%B %Y}\"\n\n\ndef _published_posts(database: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Published Posts only, newest First-published date first.\n\n    Ordered by First-published date, not by edit time, so a correction never\n    moves a Post. The byline is the Author's Display name; the Username is not\n    even selected.\n    \"\"\"\n    with closing(connect(database)) as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT posts.title, posts.slug, posts.body, posts.updated_at, \"\n            \"posts.first_published_at, users.display_name AS author_name \"\n            \"FROM posts JOIN users ON users.id = posts.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE posts.status = 'published' \"\n            \"ORDER BY posts.first_published_at DESC, posts.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    return [_post_for_template(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef _post_for_template(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:\n    posted_iso, posted_label = _day(row[\"first_published_at\"])\n    post = {\n        \"title\": row[\"title\"], \"slug\": row[\"slug\"], \"author_name\": row[\"author_name\"],\n        \"body_html\": render_body(row[\"body\"], root=\"../\"),\n        \"posted_iso\": posted_iso, \"posted_label\": posted_label,\n        \"updated_iso\": None, \"updated_label\": None,\n    }\n    if row[\"updated_at\"] > row[\"first_published_at\"]:\n        post[\"updated_iso\"], post[\"updated_label\"] = _day(row[\"updated_at\"])\n    return post\n\n\ndef copy_images(source: Path, out: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy the release-holder's approved image files to <site>/images/.\n\n    Only image files are copied (by extension), and never hidden ones, so a stray\n    `.env` or script dropped in the folder cannot reach the public site.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not source.is_dir():\n        return\n    for path in sorted(source.rglob(\"*\")):\n        relative = path.relative_to(source)\n        if (path.is_file() and path.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_SUFFIXES\n                and not any(part.startswith(\".\") for part in relative.parts)):\n            target = out / \"images\" / relative\n            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            shutil.copyfile(path, target)\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None, database: Path | None = None,\n                images: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    database = database or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    images = images or settings.IMAGES\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    (out / \"posts\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    published = _published_posts(database)\n    published_pages = pages.list_published(database)\n    # Every page of the site shows the same Navigation; the template prefixes `root`.\n    nav_pages = [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"slug\": page[\"slug\"]} for page in published_pages]\n    common = {\"site_title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"nav_pages\": nav_pages}\n\n    def write(name: str, template: str, **context) -> None:\n        (out / name).write_text(env.get_template(template).render(\n            **common, **context))\n\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text((settings.TEMPLATES / \"public\" / \"style.css\").read_text())\n    copy_images(images, out)\n    write(\"index.html\", \"public/home.html\", title=settings.SITE_TITLE, root=\"\",\n          welcome=WELCOME, posts=published[:HOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS], card_level=3)\n    write(\"announcements.html\", \"public/announcements.html\",\n          title=f\"Announcements · {settings.SITE_TITLE}\", root=\"\", posts=published,\n          current=\"announcements\")\n    for post in published:\n        write(f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\", \"public/post.html\", root=\"../\", post=post,\n              title=post[\"title\"], current=\"announcements\")\n    for page in published_pages:\n        write(f\"{page['slug']}.html\", \"public/page.html\", root=\"\", title=page[\"title\"],\n              current=page[\"slug\"],\n              page={\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"body_html\": render_body(page[\"body\"])})\n    return Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     Pages one folder down (posts/) reach the site root with a `root` of \"../\".\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import closing\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import pages, settings\nfrom app.db import connect\nfrom app.rendering import render_body\n\n# The wording comes from notes/client-brief.md. Make no other claim about ASA.\nWELCOME = (\n    \"ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African students and students \"\n    \"with African backgrounds, while welcoming anyone interested in African \"\n    \"cultures and community.\"\n)\nHOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS = 5\n# Approved image files the release-holder may add to images/. Anything else is ignored.\nIMAGE_SUFFIXES = {\".png\", \".jpg\", \".jpeg\", \".gif\", \".webp\", \".svg\"}\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef _day(timestamp: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"A stored UTC timestamp as (\"2026-09-28\", \"28 September 2026\").\"\"\"\n    moment = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp)\n    return moment.date().isoformat(), f\"{moment.day} {moment:%B %Y}\"\n\n\ndef _published_posts(database: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Published Posts only, newest First-published date first.\n\n    Ordered by First-published date, not by edit time, so a correction never\n    moves a Post. The byline is the Author's Display name; the Username is not\n    even selected.\n    \"\"\"\n    with closing(connect(database)) as conn:\n        rows = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT posts.title, posts.slug, posts.body, posts.updated_at, \"\n            \"posts.first_published_at, users.display_name AS author_name \"\n            \"FROM posts JOIN users ON users.id = posts.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE posts.status = 'published' \"\n            \"ORDER BY posts.first_published_at DESC, posts.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    return [_post_for_template(row) for row in rows]\n\n\ndef _post_for_template(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:\n    posted_iso, posted_label = _day(row[\"first_published_at\"])\n    post = {\n        \"title\": row[\"title\"], \"slug\": row[\"slug\"], \"author_name\": row[\"author_name\"],\n        \"body_html\": render_body(row[\"body\"], root=\"../\"),\n        \"posted_iso\": posted_iso, \"posted_label\": posted_label,\n        \"updated_iso\": None, \"updated_label\": None,\n    }\n    if row[\"updated_at\"] > row[\"first_published_at\"]:\n        post[\"updated_iso\"], post[\"updated_label\"] = _day(row[\"updated_at\"])\n    return post\n\n\ndef copy_images(source: Path, out: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy the release-holder's approved image files to <site>/images/.\n\n    Only image files are copied (by extension), and never hidden ones, so a stray\n    `.env` or script dropped in the folder cannot reach the public site.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not source.is_dir():\n        return\n    for path in sorted(source.rglob(\"*\")):\n        relative = path.relative_to(source)\n        if (path.is_file() and path.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_SUFFIXES\n                and not any(part.startswith(\".\") for part in relative.parts)):\n            target = out / \"images\" / relative\n            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            shutil.copyfile(path, target)\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None, database: Path | None = None,\n                images: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    database = database or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    images = images or settings.IMAGES\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    (out / \"posts\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    published = _published_posts(database)\n    published_pages = pages.list_published(database)\n    # Every page of the site shows the same Navigation; the template prefixes `root`.\n    nav_pages = [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"slug\": page[\"slug\"]} for page in published_pages]\n    common = {\"site_title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"nav_pages\": nav_pages}\n\n    def write(name: str, template: str, **context) -> None:\n        (out / name).write_text(env.get_template(template).render(\n            **common, **context))\n\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text((settings.TEMPLATES / \"public\" / \"style.css\").read_text())\n    copy_images(images, out)\n    write(\"index.html\", \"public/home.html\", title=settings.SITE_TITLE, root=\"\",\n          welcome=WELCOME, posts=published[:HOME_ANNOUNCEMENTS], card_level=3)\n    write(\"announcements.html\", \"public/announcements.html\",\n          title=f\"Announcements · {settings.SITE_TITLE}\", root=\"\", posts=published,\n          current=\"announcements\")\n    for post in published:\n        write(f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\", \"public/post.html\", root=\"../\", post=post,\n              title=post[\"title\"], current=\"announcements\")\n    for page in published_pages:\n        write(f\"{page['slug']}.html\", \"public/page.html\", root=\"\", title=page[\"title\"],\n              current=page[\"slug\"],\n              page={\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"body_html\": render_body(page[\"body\"])})\n    return The pieces already covered by the T03\ntests (five-item Home page, ordering, Updated dates) are not repeated here.\n\"\"\"\nimport importlib.util\nimport re\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import posts, settings\nfrom app.publish import IMAGE_SUFFIXES, render_site\nfrom app.rendering import render_body\nfrom tests.test_t03_publish import (WELCOME, add_post, all_text, html_files, read,\n                                    site_files, titles_in_order)\n\nBRIEF_WELCOME = (\n    \"ASA is a Kenyon student group primarily for African \"seed_demo\", settings.ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"seed_demo.py\")\nseed_demo = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)\n_spec.loader.exec_module(seed_demo)\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef images_dir(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"A release-holder's folder of approved image files.\"\"\"\n    folder = tmp_path / \"approved-images\"\n    folder.mkdir()\n    (folder / \"dance.png\").write_bytes(b\"\\x89PNG demo\")\n    (folder / \"crowd.jpg\").write_bytes(b\"jpeg demo\")\n    (folder / \"pattern.svg\").write_text(\"<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'/>\")\n    return folder\n\n\ndef publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, images):\n    return render_site(tmp_path / \"site\", database=db_path, images=images)\n\n\ndef seed_everything(db_path):\n    seed_demo.seed_demo_posts(db_path)\n    seed_demo.seed_demo_pages(db_path)\n\n\ndef visible_text(html):\n    return re.sub(r\"<[^>]+>\", \" \", html)\n\n\ndef main_nav(html):\n    return re.search(r'<nav aria-label=\"Main\">(.*?)</nav>', html, re.S).group(1)\n\n\nclass Outline(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"The headings, images and landmarks of one HTML file, in document order.\"\"\"\ndef test_home_page_welcome_uses_exactly_the_client_briefs_wording(db_path, tmp_path):\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None)\n    assert BRIEF_WELCOME in read(out, \"index.html\")\n    assert WELCOME in BRIEF_WELCOME\n\n\ndef test_the_welcome_comes_before_the_announcements(db_path, tmp_path):\n    add_post(db_path, \"Afrobeat Night\")\n    home = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), test_no_claim_about_asa_beyond_the_brief_appears_in_the_export(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    text = visible_text(all_text(out)).replace(BRIEF_WELCOME, \"\").lower()\n    for claim in CLAIMS:\n        assert claim not in text, claim\n\n\n# -- Event cards -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\nBODY_WITH_BAD_HEADINGS = \"# Big title\\n\\n#### Deep one\\n\\n## Medium\\n\\n###### Deepest\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_every_page_has_one_h1_and_headings_never_skip_a_level(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    add_post(db_path, \"Headings Post\", BODY_WITH_BAD_HEADINGS)\n    add_post(db_path, \"Another\")\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    assert len(html_files(out)) > 5\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        levels = Outline(path.read_text()).levels\n        assert levels[0] == 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n        assert levels.count(1) == 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n        for before, after in zip(levels, levels[1:]):\n            assert after <= before + 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n\n\n    assert all(image.get(\"alt\", \"\").strip() for image in Outline(page).images)\n\n\ndef test_every_page_is_a_complete_phone_friendly_document(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        html = path.read_text()\n        outline = Outline(html)\n        assert html.lower().startswith(\"<!doctype html>\"), path.name\n        assert outline.lang == \"en\", path.name\n        assert 'name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\"' in html\n        assert \"<title>\" in html and \"<main\" in html and 'aria-label=\"Main\"' in html\n\n\ndef test_there_is_a_skip_link_to_the_main_content(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        html = path.read_text()\n        link = re.search(r'<body[^>]*>\\s*<a class=\"skip-link\" href=\"#([^\"]+)\"', html)\n        assert link, path.name\n        assert f'id=\"{link.group(1)}\"' in html.split(\"<main\", 1)[1].split(\">\", 1)[0] + \">\", path.name\n\n\ndef test_the_current_page_is_marked_in_the_navigation(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for name, label in ((\"announcements.html\", \"Announcements\"), (\"photos.html\", \"Photos\"),\n                        (\"posts/afrobeat-event-demo-placeholder.html\", \"Announcements\")):\n        nav = main_nav(read(out, name))\n        current = re.findall(r'<a [^>]*aria-current=\"page\"[^>]*>([^<]+)</a>', nav)\n        assert current == [label], (name, current)\n    assert \"aria-current\" not in main_nav(read(out, \"index.html\"))\n\n\ndef _tokens(block):\n    return dict(re.findall(r\"--([\\w-]+):\\s*(#[0-9a-fA-F]{6})\", block))\n\n\ndef _luminance(hex_colour):\n    channels = [int(hex_colour[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)]\n    r, g, b = [c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for c in channels]\n    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b\n\n\ndef contrast(a, b):\n    high, low = sorted((_luminance(a), _luminance(b)), reverse=True)\n    return (high + 0.05) / (low + 0.05)\n\n\ndef test_text_and_link_colours_are_readable_in_light_and_dark(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    dark_start = css.index(\"prefers-color-scheme: dark\")\n    light, dark = _tokens(css[:dark_start]), _tokens(css[dark_start:])\n    pairs = [(\"text\", \"bg\"), (\"text\", \"surface\"), (\"muted\", \"bg\"), (\"muted\", \"surface\"),\n             (\"link\", \"bg\"), (\"link\", \"surface\"), (\"on-accent\", \"accent\"),\n             (\"focus\", \"bg\"), (\"focus\", \"surface\")]\n    for name, tokens in ((\"light\", light), (\"dark\", dark)):\n        for fore, back in pairs:\n            ratio = contrast(tokens[fore], tokens[back])\n            needed = 3.0 if fore == \"focus\" else 4.5\n            assert ratio >= needed, f\"{name}: {fore} on {back} is {ratio:.2f}:1\"\n\n\ndef test_focus_is_visible_and_the_layout_adapts_to_a_phone(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    assert \":focus-visible\" in css\n    assert \"outline: none\" not in css and \"outline:none\" not in css\n    assert re.search(r\"img\\s*\\{[^}]*max-width:\\s*100%\", css)\n    for width in re.findall(r\"(?<!max-)(?<!-)width:\\s*(\\d+)px\", css):\n        assert int(width) <= 390, f\"fixed width {width}px\"\n\n\ndef test_nothing_in_the_styles_loads_from_outside_the_site(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    assert \"http\" not in css and \"@import\" not in css and \"url(/\" not in css\n\n\n# -- Relative paths and Drafts, over the whole seeded export -------------------------\n\ndef test_the_whole_seeded_export_is_relative_and_has_no_drafts(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        for value in re.findall(r'(?:href|src)=\"([^\"]*)\"', path.read_text()):\n            assert not value.startswith(\"/\"), f\"{path.name}: {value}\"\n    text = all_text(out)\n    assert \"Draft idea\" not in text and \"Get involved\" not in text\n \"Another\")\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    assert len(html_files(out)) > 5\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        levels = Outline(path.read_text()).levels\n        assert levels[0] == 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n        assert levels.count(1) == 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n        for before, after in zip(levels, levels[1:]):\n            assert after <= before + 1, f\"{path.name}: {levels}\"\n\n\n    assert all(image.get(\"alt\", \"\").strip() for image in Outline(page).images)\n\n\ndef test_every_page_is_a_complete_phone_friendly_document(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        html = path.read_text()\n        outline = Outline(html)\n        assert html.lower().startswith(\"<!doctype html>\"), path.name\n        assert outline.lang == \"en\", path.name\n        assert 'name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\"' in html\n        assert \"<title>\" in html and \"<main\" in html and 'aria-label=\"Main\"' in html\n\n\ndef test_there_is_a_skip_link_to_the_main_content(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        html = path.read_text()\n        link = re.search(r'<body[^>]*>\\s*<a class=\"skip-link\" href=\"#([^\"]+)\"', html)\n        assert link, path.name\n        assert f'id=\"{link.group(1)}\"' in html.split(\"<main\", 1)[1].split(\">\", 1)[0] + \">\", path.name\n\n\ndef test_the_current_page_is_marked_in_the_navigation(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for name, label in ((\"announcements.html\", \"Announcements\"), (\"photos.html\", \"Photos\"),\n                        (\"posts/afrobeat-event-demo-placeholder.html\", \"Announcements\")):\n        nav = main_nav(read(out, name))\n        current = re.findall(r'<a [^>]*aria-current=\"page\"[^>]*>([^<]+)</a>', nav)\n        assert current == [label], (name, current)\n    assert \"aria-current\" not in main_nav(read(out, \"index.html\"))\n\n\ndef _tokens(block):\n    return dict(re.findall(r\"--([\\w-]+):\\s*(#[0-9a-fA-F]{6})\", block))\n\n\ndef _luminance(hex_colour):\n    channels = [int(hex_colour[i:i + 2], 16) / 255 for i in (1, 3, 5)]\n    r, g, b = [c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for c in channels]\n    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b\n\n\ndef contrast(a, b):\n    high, low = sorted((_luminance(a), _luminance(b)), reverse=True)\n    return (high + 0.05) / (low + 0.05)\n\n\ndef test_text_and_link_colours_are_readable_in_light_and_dark(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    dark_start = css.index(\"prefers-color-scheme: dark\")\n    light, dark = _tokens(css[:dark_start]), _tokens(css[dark_start:])\n    pairs = [(\"text\", \"bg\"), (\"text\", \"surface\"), (\"muted\", \"bg\"), (\"muted\", \"surface\"),\n             (\"link\", \"bg\"), (\"link\", \"surface\"), (\"on-accent\", \"accent\"),\n             (\"focus\", \"bg\"), (\"focus\", \"surface\")]\n    for name, tokens in ((\"light\", light), (\"dark\", dark)):\n        for fore, back in pairs:\n            ratio = contrast(tokens[fore], tokens[back])\n            needed = 3.0 if fore == \"focus\" else 4.5\n            assert ratio >= needed, f\"{name}: {fore} on {back} is {ratio:.2f}:1\"\n\n\ndef test_focus_is_visible_and_the_layout_adapts_to_a_phone(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    assert \":focus-visible\" in css\n    assert \"outline: none\" not in css and \"outline:none\" not in css\n    assert re.search(r\"img\\s*\\{[^}]*max-width:\\s*100%\", css)\n    for width in re.findall(r\"(?<!max-)(?<!-)width:\\s*(\\d+)px\", css):\n        assert int(width) <= 390, f\"fixed width {width}px\"\n\n\ndef test_nothing_in_the_styles_loads_from_outside_the_site(db_path, tmp_path):\n    css = read(publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, None), \"style.css\")\n    assert \"http\" not in css and \"@import\" not in css and \"url(/\" not in css\n\n\n# -- Relative paths and Drafts, over the whole seeded export -------------------------\n\ndef test_the_whole_seeded_export_is_relative_and_has_no_drafts(db_path, tmp_path):\n    seed_everything(db_path)\n    out = publish_with(db_path, tmp_path, settings.IMAGES)\n    for path in html_files(out):\n        for value in re.findall(r'(?:href|src)=\"([^\"]*)\"', path.read_text()):\n            assert not value.startswith(\"/\"), f\"{path.name}: {value}\"\n    text = all_text(out)\n    assert \"Draft idea\" not in text and \"Get involved\" not in text\n    assert not any(\"draft\" in p.name or \"get-involved\" in p.name for p in site_files(out))\n    assert titles_in_order(read(out, \"announcements.html\")) == [\n        \"Afrobeat event (demo The one path for the public export and, later, Preview.\n\nRaw HTML is let through the Markdown parser and then removed by the sanitizer,\nso `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<form>` and event handlers never survive. Only\nheadings, emphasis, lists, links and images (with alt text) are kept.\n\nTwo things keep the page accessible whatever an Editor types: headings in a Body\nare moved below the page's own <h1> without skipping a level, and an image with\nno alt text gets a plain fallback instead of none.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\nimport nh3\n\n_markdown = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\", {\"html\": True})\n\n_TAGS = {\n    \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"p\", \"br\", \"em\", \"strong\",\n    \"ul\", \"ol\", \"li\", \"a\", \"img\",\n}\n_ATTRIBUTES = {\"a\": {\"href\", \"title\"}, \"img\": {\"src\", \"alt\", \"title\"}}\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"http\", \"https\", \"mailto\"}\n\n# Approved image files are copied to <site>/images/. An Editor always writes\n# `images/<file>`; each page adds the `root` that gets from there to the site root.\nNO_ALT = \"Image without a description\"\n\n_HEADING = re.compile(r\"<(/?)h([1-6])>\")\n_IMG_WITHOUT_ALT = re.compile(r\"<img(?![^>]*\\salt=)\")\n# `images/x.png`, `./images/x.png` and `../images/x.png` all mean the approved-images folder.\n_IMAGES_REFERENCE = re.compile(r\"^(?:\\.{1,2}/)*(images/.*)$\", re.S)\n\n\ndef _attribute_filter(root: str):\n    def keep(tag: str, name: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Drop root-absolute links and images (the site is served from a\n        subfolder), point `images/...` at the site root, and never leave alt empty.\"\"\"\n        if name in (\"href\", \"src\") and value.strip().startswith(\"/\"):\n            return None\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"src\":\n            reference = _IMAGES_REFERENCE.match(value)\n            if reference:\n                return root + reference.group(1)\n        if tag == \"img\" and name == \"alt\" and not value.strip():\n            return NO_ALT\n        return value\n\n    return keep\n\n\ndef _nest_headings(html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Body headings start at <h2> and never skip a level.\n\n    The page's own title is the only <h1>. A heading may be at most one level\n    deeper than the one before it; siblings stay siblings.\n    \"\"\"\n    last_level = 1      # the page's own <h1>\n    open_level = 2      # level of the heading currently open\n\n    def fix(match: re.Match) -> str:\n        nonlocal last_level, open_level\n        if match.group(1):\n            return f\"</h{open_level}>\"\n        open_level = min(max(int(match.group(2)), 2), last_level + 1)\n        last_level = open_level\n        return f\"<h{open_level}>\"\n\n    return _HEADING.sub(fix, html)\n\n\ndef render_body(markdown: str, root: str = \"\") -> str:\n    \"\"\"`root` is the relative path from the page to the site root (\"\" or \"../\").\"\"\"\n    html = nh3.clean(\n        _markdown.render(markdown),\n        tags=_TAGS,\n        attributes=_ATTRIBUTES,\n        url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES,\n        clean_content_tags={\"script\", \"style\", \"iframe\", \"form\"},\n        attribute_filter=_attribute_filter(root),\n    )\n    html = _IMG_WITHOUT_ALT.sub(f'<img alt=\"{NO_ALT}\"', html)\n    return _nest_headings(html)\n# Copy to .env (which is gitignored) and change the values.\n# Load it with `uv run --env-file .env ...`; the app reads only the environment.\nCMS_SECRET_KEY=change-me-to-a-long-random-string\nCMS_SITE_TITLE=African Student Association\nCMS_DATABASE=cms.db\n# Set after you deploy, e.g. https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nCMS_BASE_PATH=\nT06-content-list-390px.png\nT06-dashboard-390px.png\nT07-home-390px.png\nT07-photos-390px.png\n/Users/yawoppong-krampah/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/node\n/Users/yawoppong-krampah/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/bin/npx\nchromium not found\ngoogle-chrome not found\nGoogle Chrome 2.app\nGoogle Chrome 3.app\nGoogle Chrome.app\ngooglechrome.dmg","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a417abae-8984-467b-a665-290aba0d92b8","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:39:52.593Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Markdown Body -> safe HTML. /* the title link stretches over the whole card */\n  display: flex;\n  flex-direction: column;\n  gap: 0.4rem;\n  padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem 1.25rem;\n  background: var(--surface);\n  border: 1px solid }\n\n.card-dates { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem 0.5rem; margin: 0; font-size: 0.95rem; }\n.chip {\n  display: inline-block;\n  padding: 0.05rem 0.6rem;\n }\n.card-more { margin: auto 0 0; padding-top: 0.5rem; color: var(--link); font-weight: 700; }\n\n.meta { margin: 0.35rem 0 1.25rem; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.95rem; }\n\n.body > :first-child
