No external files.\n   Every text/background pair below is checked for contrast by tests/test_t07_public_site.py. */\n:root {\n  color-scheme: light;\n  --bg: #fbf7f0;\n  --surface: #ffffff;\n  --text: #1f1a14;\n  --muted: #5b5247;\n  --link: #8a2d0f;\n  --accent: #8a2d0f;\n  --on-accent: #ffffff;\n  --focus: #0b57d0;\n  --line: #d9cfc0;\n  --band-1: #8a2d0f;\n  --band-2: #c8941f;\n  --band-3: #2f6b3f;\n}\n\n@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {\n  :root {\n    color-scheme: dark;\n    --bg: #17130f;\n    --surface: #231d17;\n    --text: #f3ece2;\n    --muted: #c4b8a8;\n    --link: #f2a07b;\n    --accent: #f2a07b;\n    --on-accent: #17130f;\n    --focus: #8ab4f8;\n    --line: #4a3f33;\n    --band-1: #f2a07b;\n    --band-2: #e0b54a;\n    --band-3: #6fb583;\n  }\n}\n\n*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }\n\nhtml { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; }\n\nbody {\n  margin: 0;\n  background: var(--bg);\n  color: var(--text);\n  font: 1.0625rem/1.65 system-ui, -apple-system, \"Segoe UI\", sans-serif;\n  overflow-wrap: anywhere;\n}\n\nimg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }\n\na { color: var(--link); text-underline-offset: 0.15em; }\na:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 0.15em; }\n\n:focus-visible {\n  outline: 3px solid var(--focus);\n  outline-offset: 3px;\n  border-radius: 2px;\n}\n\n.skip-link {\n  position: absolute;\n  left: 1rem;\n  top: -4rem;\n  z-index: 10;\n  padding: 0.6rem 1rem;\n  background: var(--accent);\n  color: var(--on-accent);\n  font-weight: 700;\n}\n.skip-link:focus { top: 0.5rem; }\n\n/* Header: a decorative colour band, the site name, then the Navigation. */\n.site-header { border-top: 0.5rem solid var(--band-1); border-image: linear-gradient(\n  to right, var(--band-1) 0 33%, var(--band-2) 33% 66%, var(--band-3) 66% 100%) 1; }\n.site-header-inner { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0.75rem 1rem 0; }\n.site-name {\n  display: inline-block;\n  padding: 0.4rem 0;\n  color: var(--text);\n  font-size: 1.15rem;\n  font-weight: 800;\n  text-decoration: none;\n}\n.site-header nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem 0.5rem; margin: 0 -0.5rem; }\n.site-header nav a {\n  display: inline-block;\n  padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem;          /* a comfortable touch target */\n  color: var(--text);\n  font-weight: 600;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  border-bottom: 3px solid transparent;\n}\n.site-header nav a:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--line); }\n.site-header nav a[aria-current=\"page\"] { color: var(--link); border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }\n\nmain { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 1.5rem 1rem 2.5rem; }\n\nh1 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1.9rem; line-height: 1.2; }\nh2 { margin: 2rem 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1.45rem; line-height: 1.25; }\nh3 { margin: 1.5rem 0 0.5rem; font-size: 1.2rem; line-height: 1.3; }\nh4, h5, h6 { margin: 1.25rem 0 0.5rem; font-size: 1.05rem; }\n\n.hero {\n  margin-bottom: 1.5rem;\n  padding: 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.5rem;\n  background: var(--surface);\n  border: 1px solid var(--line);\n  border-left: 0.5rem solid var(--accent);\n  border-radius: 0.5rem;\n}\n.welcome { margin: 0; font-size: 1.15rem; }\n\n.cards { margin-block: 1rem; }\n.card {\n  margin-block: 1rem;\n  padding: 1rem 1.1rem;\n  background: var(--surface);\n  border: 1px solid var(--line);\n  border-radius: 0.5rem;\n}\n.card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.3; }\n.card-title a { color: var(--text); text-decoration-color: var(--accent); }\n.card-title a:hover { color: var(--link); }\n.meta { margin: 0.35rem 0 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.95rem; }\n\n.more {\n  display: inline-block;\n  margin-top: 0.5rem;\n  padding: 0.7rem 1.1rem;\n  background: var(--accent);\n  color: var(--on-accent);\n  font-weight: 700;\n  text-decoration: none;\n  border-radius: 0.4rem;\n}\n.more:hover { text-decoration: underline; }\n\n.body > :first-child { margin-top: 0; }\n.body img { display: block; margin-block: 1rem 0.25rem; border-radius: 0.4rem; }\n.body em { color: var(--muted); }\n.body ul, .body ol { padding-left: 1.4rem; }\n\n.back { margin-top: 2rem; }\n\nfooter { max-width: 44rem; margin: 0 auto; padding: 1rem 1rem 2rem; color: var(--muted); border-top: 1px solid var(--line); }\n\n@media (min-width: 40rem) {\n  h1 { font-size: 2.3rem; The navigation shows only Announcements, because your `cms.db` has **0 Pages**.\n- **http://localhost:8002** is a scratch copy of your DB with only the three starter Pages added. This is what the site looks like once About ASA, Resources and Photos are Published.\n\nI was wrong earlier when I said your Photos page had an \"old body\". There is no Photos page in your database at all.\n\n## What changed\n- **Style:** a warm cream and terracotta palette with gold and green accents. Headings are serif and body text is sans-serif, all system fonts with nothing loaded from outside.\n- **Header and hero:** the header now shows only a short \"ASA\" mark, so the full name appears once, in the hero heading. Your `.env` title is \"ASA — African Student Association\", so \"ASA\" still shows twice. Changing `CMS_SITE_TITLE` to just the full name would fix that.\n- **Illustration:** an original inline SVG of a sun over layered hills and a diamond band. It is marked decorative and carries no claim about real ASA events.\n- **Event cards:**\n  - Each card now has a \"Posted\" chip (plus \"Updated\" when it applies), the byline, a short excerpt, and a \"Read the announcement →\" cue.\n  - The whole card is clickable. The date is never labelled as the event date.\n- **Instagram:** `https://www.instagram.com/asa.kenyon/` is linked from the hero button and the footer on every page.\n\n## Checks\n- **Layout:** no horizontal overflow on any of the six pages at 390, 768 or 1280 px. My first 390 px screenshots looked clipped, but that was headless Chrome's minimum window width. Re-measured through a real 390 px frame, they are fine.\n- **Keyboard:** the tab order is skip link, brand, the nav links, page content, then footer. Every focusable element shows a focus ring. I raised the post page's \"All announcements\" link above the 24 px minimum target height.\n- **Contrast:** all colour pairs, light and dark, are checked by tests at 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for focus. I viewed the dark scheme in a forced-dark render, because headless Chrome ignored the dark-mode flag.\n- **New tests:** the full name appearing once, the Instagram link, the decorative illustration, the three-page navigation, and the card content.\n\n## Your decision: adding the Pages\nTo show About ASA, Resources and Photos in your real site, the starter Pages must be added to `cms.db`. I haven't done it, since you asked me to preserve the database. The safe route is a pages-only seed, which skips accounts and Posts. I'd back up `cms.db` first. Alternatively you can create the three Pages in the admin console. Tell me which you prefer.\n\n## Heads-up\nThe `notes/usage-ledger.csv` change and the transcripts are still uncommitted from before. Accounts and Posts were verified byte-identical before and after. The draft demo Page was deliberately not added. {"parentUuid":"10090c11-431a-4fee-bcf1-3d9a046717d3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"969dc776-3cb5-420d-a3a6-6545f11f23b2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yawoppong-krampah/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the working tree against HEAD (b29a37c, the pushed T07 commit). The spec is GitHub issue #10 (T07b), plus CLAUDE.md hard constraints, CONTEXT.md, and the original T07 acceptance criteria in issue #8. Exclude notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/ from the review: they are not part of this change."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"6291c5a4-c4d2-4fa7-86cb-b0b84b53de44","timestamp":"2026-10-13T00:46:32.334Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01TigSyLBXvrVFpvBcELtGto","session_id":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"b68357c6-d59e-4995-a597-7ee18ee605d2","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Spec review of the uncommitted redesign diff against issue #10 (T07b), issue #8 (T07) and the glossary**\n\n`uv run pytest -q` passes (315). I probed `_excerpt` with headings, images, lists, entities, an empty body, code and long words, and found no excerpt bugs.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- Issue #10 says the Instagram link is in \"the hero and the footer of every page\". The hero link is on Home only (`templates/public/home.html:11`). Other pages get the footer link only (`templates/public/base.html:24`). The test (`tests/test_t07_public_site.py:392`) only requires one link per page, so the claim is only half true.\n- #10 says \"a visible focus ring on every focusable element\". `.card-title a:focus-visible { outline-color: transparent }` (`style.css:253`) hides the link's own ring. The card ring depends on `.card:has(a:focus-visible)` (`style.css:234`). In browsers without `:has()`, such as Firefox before 121, a focused card shows no ring. This claim is not tested at all.\n- #10 says \"Contrast: every text/background token pair\". Colours with no tested pair include `.hero` `--art-*` and the `.button-outline` border. Hover states and the `.card-more` text are untested too. \"Every\" overstates what is covered.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n- `scroll-behavior: smooth` (`style.css:61`) has no `prefers-reduced-motion` guard. This is a small accessibility regression, and the user didn't ask for it.\n- Not requested: the \"See the latest announcements\" CTA (`home.html:10`), the \"Welcome\" eyebrow, the rotating card border colours (`style.css:231-232`), the hover lift (`style.css:298`), and the new `CMS_SITE_SHORT_TITLE` and `CMS_INSTAGRAM_URL` env settings.\n- The full dark-palette overhaul and the `.env` edit are also outside the request. #10 does disclose the `.env` change.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but is wrong or weak**\n- `tests/test_t07_public_site.py:406` asserts `\"photo\" not in visible_text(home).lower()`. It passes only because that test publishes no Pages. With the seeded \"Photos\" nav link it would fail, so it doesn't test a real constraint. The visible text is also the wrong thing to check, because the SVG is `aria-hidden`.\n- The #8 requirement for no claim beyond the brief is untested for the new copy. That copy is \"Follow @asa.kenyon on Instagram\", the eyebrow and the CTA. #10 admits the account was never verified.\n- The `style.css:162` comment says \"full-width warm band\". The hero is a rounded box inside `main` (`max-width: 64rem`), and `.hero-inner` repeats that max-width. The `border-bottom` with `border-radius` also renders a curved bar.\n- Excerpt tests (`tests/test_t07_public_site.py:417` and `:426`) cover only one happy path and one long case. There are no cases for a heading-first body (which gives \"What Party at…\", with no punctuation between heading and text), an image-only body, an empty body or entities.\n- The ellipsis cut (`app/publish.py:76`) drops the last whole word when the 140th character is already a word boundary.\n- `.site-name` reads \"ASA home\" (`base.html:13`), which is fine. But the full name now appears nowhere on non-Home pages except `&lt;title&gt;`, so a visitor landing on a Post never sees \"African Student Association\" in the page body. This follows from the user's \"avoid repeating\" request but is worth knowing.\n\n**Still holds:**\n- The Welcome text is unchanged, and the five Home cards are intact.\n- Cards show \"Posted\" and \"Updated\" with no event-date label.\n- Home heading order is h1, then h2, then h3 cards, because `card_level=3` is still passed.\n- There is one h1 per page.\n- The SVG is `aria-hidden` and `focusable=\"false\"`.\n- All paths are relative.\n- Navigation behaviour is unchanged.\n- No `&lt;img&gt;` appears in the hero.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>53290</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>6</tool_uses><duration_ms>117963</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}
